Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 4 and the pivotal run chase is also about to get underway. Earlier in the break, the light roller was used but now it is all up to the players from both teams. The umpires are out in the middle and so is the Indian opening pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and skipper Rohit Sharma. It will be Joe Root who will take the new ball for England. Let's play...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Right then, as England are bowled out for 420 runs, Lunch has been taken and when India come back out, they will have to chase down 231 runs for the win which will be one of the highest-successful run chases in the final innings on Indian soil. England now have a lot to bowl at but their spinners really need to make an impact and Joe Root will be crucial with the ball in hand. A Test match that is brilliantly poised and we couldn't have asked for more. Do join us in about half an hours time for the exciting run chase.

India seemed to have the game well in control in the first two days of the Test match but have been frustrated for more than a day by an English side that simply doesn't give up. The spinners were put under pressure and couldn't get the same purchase like they did in the first innings but Jasprit Bumrah stood out as he bowled extremely well and got wickets at crucial stages of the game. A couple of catches were dropped and the fielders looked lethargic but after a lot of resistance, they were able to pick up the final three wickets in a jiffy. Bumrah ended with four wickets and now, the onus is on the Indian openers to give their side a good start.

Wow, that was some innings from Ollie Pope and he will be devastated to have fallen just of a double hundred here and the crowd rightly gives him a big standing ovation. One of the best innings you will see from a touring batter and that too in the second innings but India have finally managed to take wickets in clusters and have kept the English lead to well below the 250-run mark. The final lead stands at 230 runs which is still pretty massive to get beyond in the final innings of a Test match on a turning track. It was a fine first session for England as both Rehan Ahmed and Tom Hartley were able to build stands with Pope who kept on playing his shots. Hartley in particular played very well and that should give him confidence with the ball as well.

OUT! TIMBER! Jasprit Bumrah outsmarts Ollie Pope on this occasion to bring an end to the England innings! Bowls a slower ball, pitched right up on the off stump line. Ollie Pope looks to play the reverse scoop as he expected it to be a fast yorker but misses the ball completely due to the lack of pace on the ball. The ball hits the off stump and India ends the innings. A superb innings from the England vice-captain, Ollie Pope comes to an end.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set as the Players and the Umpires are out in the field to start the Day 4 of this Test match. Ollie Pope and Rehan Ahmed walk out to bat for England. Ravindra Jadeja to start the attack for India. Let's Play!

The day promises to be a superb one for cricket as the Test match still hangs in the balance. Will India be able to get the wickets soon and come out to start their chase in the first session itself? Or will Ollie Pope be the star for England and bat through the innings to take his team to a good second-innings score? Let’s find out as the Day 3 of this 1st Test between England and India, starts soon. Stay tuned.

India, after being on top for the first 2 days suffered a setback yesterday with both bat and ball. They were all out in the first hour of the match and then leaked a lot of runs during their bowling. Jasprit Bumrah has been the pick of the Indian bowlers as he not only has picked 2 very important wickets but also has been very economical and has bowled according to the plan. India will be eager to bounce back and get the English batter all out before they touch the 200 mark. Regardless, they will have to bat really well to chase down anything over 150 as the wicket is becoming more and more favorable to the spinners. India has the second new ball due in the next three overs and will be formulating all their plans keeping that in mind.

A very good morning to each and everyone joining us here today on Day 4 of this 1st Test Match between India and England where England in their second innings is 316/6 after 77 overs bowled and currently holds a lead of 126 runs. England won the toss and chose to Bat first and was able to put a first-innings score of 246. India in reply scored 436 runs getting a first innings lead of 190 runs. England came out to bat positive yesterday and are eyeing a lead of over 200 runs and looking at the way the wicket is playing, it is going to be a par total for India to chase. Ollie Pope, England’s number 3 is still at the crease batting at 148 not out overnight score, and along with him is the young Rehan Ahmed batting on the overnight score of 16. England at one point were 163/5 when Ollie Pope and Ben Foakes stitched up a 100-run partnership before Ben Foakes was dismissed by Axar Patel in the final hour of the match. England currently holds a strong position and will be looking to capitalise and turn the game in their favor. The first session is going to be a very important one for both teams.
... DAY 4, FIRST SESSION ...

Right then, England leads by 126 runs and will be looking to go past the 200-run mark if they want their bowlers to have a chance to get India all out before that as there are still 2 days left in the Test match. India will be looking to regroup as a bowling side and will be looking to execute the plans better. Day 4 will begin on Sunday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT) but you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Cheers!

Zak Crawley is down for a chat. He says that they are very happy and Ollie Pope played a wonderful knock and a few more runs and it could be a tricky chase. Adds that the process was to play good cricketing shots and on his dismissal he says that Ashwin bowled a good ball and there's nothing he can do about it. Mentions that the lines the bowlers bowled allowed them to go for the reverse sweep more and ends by saying that they would have taken a lead of 100 runs but will now look to add 40-50 more runs.

India finds itself reflecting on missed opportunities and areas for improvement in their performance. While the day witnessed commendable efforts from the Indian bowlers, the team would have aspired for a more productive outcome, both in terms of wickets taken and runs conceded. Throughout the day's play, the Indian bowling unit struggled with consistency, proving to be expensive at times and failing to apply sustained pressure on the English batters. Additionally, lapses in fielding, falling below international standards, compounded India's challenges, with missed opportunities, such as the dropped catch of Ollie Pope by Axar Patel at point, proving costly. Furthermore, the bowlers' inability to maintain pressure and restrict boundaries allowed England to build momentum, posing a significant challenge for India's quest to regain control of the match. Notably, Ravindra Jadeja's uncharacteristic tally of seven no-balls further added to India's woes, highlighting the need for greater discipline and focus in their bowling efforts. With the Test match hanging in the balance, India recognizes the importance of a proactive approach on the field from the onset of play tomorrow. The team will be eager to rectify their shortcomings, striving for improved bowling accuracy, tighter fielding, and enhanced focus to create opportunities and mount a spirited comeback in pursuit of victory.

As the sun sets on the third day of this gripping Test match, the equilibrium of the contest remains delicately poised, with England emerging as the dominant force, posting a formidable total of 316/3 in 77 overs and securing a crucial lead of 126 runs. Today belonged unequivocally to England, who exhibited resilience and determination reminiscent of a champion team. Commencing their resurgence by swiftly dismissing the Indian side in the opening hour, England then showcased their batting prowess, defying the challenges posed by the experienced Indian bowling attack to establish a commanding position in the match. At the forefront of England's resurgence stands Ollie Pope, whose masterful innings of 148 runs off 208 balls epitomizes excellence and grit, currently in support of the promising Rehan Ahmed. With their sights set on extending their lead beyond the 200-run mark, England's performance today stands as a testament to their perseverance and skill.

... DAY 3, THIRD SESSION ...

India will be delighted with that session as they have been able to make inroads and have dismissed all of the dangerous batters. The second started in a similar way to much of the previous one with the Indian spinners being put away for boundaries but then Jasprit Bumrah came back into the attack and made things happen as the ball started to reverse a bit. Bumrah knocked over Ben Duckett after not going upstairs for a clear LBW and looked very pumped up and then he also sent the mighty Joe Root packing. Later on, Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja bowled good spells and picked up a crucial wicket each to hand their side a big advantage. India only lead by just 18 more runs but will be hoping to pick up all five remaining wickets in the final session and chase down as small a total as possible. Join us in about 15 minutes for the final session on Day 3.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 83 runs and 4 wickets. Not the session England would have wanted as they have lost 4 wickets and after a wonderful start and they are well behind the eight ball once again. They were 89/1 coming into the second session and both Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope started off well, playing their shots and raking in the runs but then Duckett was cleaned up by Bumrah and Joe Root fell prey to the same man a few minutes later. Pope held one end well and @jon gave him good support by playing with a clear mind. However, the latter was bamboozled by a beauty from Jadeja and then skipper Ben Stokes too was bowled, leaving Pope stranded at one end and 67 unbeaten runs to his name. Ben Foakes is alongside Pope and this pair is now very crucial for England.

The Indian bowlers have not been up to the mark this first hour. They have been leaking boundaries almost every over and have been under pressure since the start of the English second innings. Ravichandran Ashwin was the only one to grab a wicket of Zak Crawley and since then, there have been some easy runs scored by the English batters. Rohit Sharma and the team have a lot to talk about during LUNCH and formulate a game plan to stop the flow of runs and pick up some good wickets to get back to the driver's seat in the Match. SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs 104 runs 4 wickets. The first session on Day 3 comes to an end where England in their second Innings are 89 after 15 overs with one wicket down still trailing by 101 runs. Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope are at the crease building a decent partnership and are batting really well. They have been scoring at a very good rate and have walked out to play positive cricket. Bringing out all the types of sweeps to counter the Indian spinners is working well and scoring a boundary in every over is getting them closer to the lead very quickly. The English batters are executing their plans well and look really comfortable at the moment. They came out today bowling with a plan and got India all out in the first hour and then battled brilliantly in the second, giving them their first session win of this match.
A single to end a productive session for England and they are 89/1 on the stroke of Lunch on Day 3. A bit too short and on leg stump, worked away 'round the corner for yet another single.
